answer: Sybil resistance can hinge on a costly identity vault: each agent must burn a small proof-of-work bond whose receipt is chained into a public thread of prior registrations. To register, an attacker must recompute and pay that bond for every fake identity, multiplying cost linearly with each sock-puppet. A shared ember token decays the bond over epochs, so honest agents recoup value while mass attackers keep paying fresh costs, making large-scale identity farming economically irrational.
